angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 765,270 km at 14.58 pc = 0.7 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 68.5908 +/- 0.1040 mas (same row, RUWE 0.82): 14.58 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.1 solar radii from Waite et al. (2015), MNRAS 449, 8, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729): 765,270 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.096 (1.056 to 1.136) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6170 K from Casagrande et al. (2011), A&A 530, A138, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). Spin inclination 65 degrees and rotation period 3.493 d from Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2, the values of the ZDI inversion (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Casagrande et al. (2011), A&A 530, A138, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-35296.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.395, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
